newsitem.title: USA: Toys acquiring Baby in stock deal.
newsitem.headline: Toys acquiring Baby in stock deal.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc will acquire Baby Superstore Inc in a stock merger valued at about $376 million, the companies said.

Under the terms of the Agreement, Baby Superstore shareholders will receive 0.8121 of a share of Toys R Us stock for each Baby Superstore share, valued at $23.45 as of the close of business on October 1, 1996.
The merger, which has been approved by both boards of directors, is subject to customary regulatory approvals and approval by Baby Superstore shareholders.
Jack Tate, founder, chairman and chief executive of Baby Superstore, will receive 0.5150 of a share for each Baby Superstore share, valued at $14.87 as of close of business on October 1, 1996.

Toys R Us Chief Executive Michael Goldstein described the transaction as "another important step in our long range strategic business plan to become the leading retailer in the infant-through-toddler marketplace. Through the excellent strategic fit of this acquisition, we will be able to accelerate our planned growth in sales and profitability of Babies "R" Us, our new format that is already exhibiting exciting growth potential."

Toys R Us said that through its acquisition of Baby Superstore, an operator of infant and toddler superstores, Babies R Us will emerge as the sector's leading specialty store operator with 73 stores in 23 states generating sales in excess of $450 million in 1996.
"The company expects the combination of these two businesses will provide significant synergies to both businesses, including lower costs and economies of scale," Goldstein said.
Goldstein also said he expected the acquisition to provide incremental sales and earnings growth to Toys R Us, "immediately following consummation of the transaction."
The deal is expected to close around the end of the companies' fiscal year at the end of January.
Tate, holder of about 46.8 percent of Baby Superstore common stock, has entered into an agreement to vote his shares in favor of the merger.

Goldman, Sachs & Co. served as financial advisers to Toys "R" Us for purposes of this transaction,m the companies said. CS First Boston and Invemed Associates Inc. served as financial advisors to Baby Superstore.
